description: imbh — embeddable observability database as a Docker log driver

env.name: IMBH_DOCKER_PLUGIN_SOCKET
env.description: Where imbhd serves the log-driver plugin API. Must match interface.socket.

env.name: IMBH_LISTEN_ADDR
env.description: OTLP/HTTP ingest + SQL query endpoint. `auto` binds every bridge network this daemon has, discovered at run time and kept up to date as networks come and go -- reachable from containers on any of them, and not from the LAN. `auto:PORT` picks the port; a literal HOST:PORT binds exactly that; a comma-separated list mixes them. Set to the empty string to open no TCP port at all.

env.name: IMBH_GRPC_LISTEN_ADDR
env.description: OTLP/gRPC ingest (the default transport for most OTel SDKs), same addressing rules as IMBH_LISTEN_ADDR -- `auto` there means every bridge gateway on port 4317. Empty disables it.

env.name: IMBH_ALLOW_FROM
env.description: Which peers the TCP listeners serve. `any` (the default) filters nothing. `docker` accepts only the daemon's own bridge subnets plus loopback -- worth setting, because /admin/* is unauthenticated and binding a bridge gateway makes it reachable by every container on the box. A comma-separated list of CIDRs narrows it further, and may include `docker` as one element (e.g. `docker,10.0.0.0/8`). A refused peer is closed on accept, before any request is read.

env.name: IMBH_DOCKER_API
env.description: Where to reach the Docker Engine API, which is what lets discovery name the networks a container is on and add container.network.* attributes to its logs. `auto` (the default) probes DOCKER_HOST and the well-known socket paths on every refresh; a path names a socket; `off` disables it. A managed plugin has no socket mounted unless you add one, so this normally falls back to the interface scan -- which still finds every bridge gateway and subnet. See docs/DOCKER_LOG_DRIVER.md.

env.name: IMBH_DOCKER_VM_NET
env.description: Whether `auto` also binds the VM's host-facing interface. Only matters on Docker Desktop, where the daemon runs inside a VM: the bridge gateways are reachable from containers, but Docker Desktop's own gateway.docker.internal / host.docker.internal names lead to the VM's uplink instead, which no bridge bind answers on. `auto` (the default) adds that address when this process is running inside a Docker Desktop VM and changes nothing anywhere else; `on` adds it on any host -- do not set it on a LAN-connected Linux server, where the same interface is the LAN and /admin/* is unauthenticated; `off` never adds it. The interface is the one the kernel's own routing table would send a packet out of, policy rules included.

env.name: IMBH_DOCKER_NETWORK_REFRESH
env.description: How often the daemon's bridge networks are re-read, which is how `auto` notices a network created or destroyed after startup. `0` discovers once at startup and never looks again.

env.name: IMBH_DOCKER_NETWORK_ATTRS
env.description: Whether stored records carry container.network.names and container.network.<name>.ip resource attributes (and .info.networks in a remap script). `on` (the default) adds them whenever discovery can name the networks a container is on, which needs the Engine API -- see IMBH_DOCKER_API. `off` never adds them. A container that starts between two refreshes has no network attributes on its first lines and gains them on the rest: the driver never asks the daemon about a container from inside the handler that is starting it, because that can deadlock the daemon against its own log driver.

env.name: IMBH_FLUSH
env.description: When buffered rows are sealed into Parquet segments (which is also what lets the WAL be reclaimed). Triggers OR together: interval=5s, buffer=16MiB, rows=50000, wal=64MiB, idle=2s, tick=250ms. `manual` seals only on POST /admin/flush and shutdown.

env.name: IMBH_DOCKER_REMAP
env.description: VRL script applied to every container line before it is stored, mapping the Docker log-driver data model onto the OpenTelemetry logs data model. `default` is the built-in remapper (JSON, logfmt, klog/glog, key=value); `off` stores lines exactly as the container printed them; `@PATH` reads a script from a path inside the plugin -- /var/lib/imbh is the daemon-provisioned database directory and persists, so @/var/lib/imbh/remap/app.vrl works once you place the file there (see docs/DOCKER_LOG_DRIVER.md); anything else is treated as an inline script. Override per container with --log-opt imbh-remap=...

env.name: IMBH_MAINTENANCE_INTERVAL
env.description: How often the retention policy is applied.

env.name: IMBH_HEADER_TIMEOUT
env.description: Total time an HTTP client gets to deliver a request line and headers before it is answered 408 and disconnected. Bounds what one idle client can hold, since the server is thread-per-connection. `0` disables it.

env.name: IMBH_BODY_TIMEOUT
env.description: How long a single read of an HTTP request body -- or a single write of a response -- may stall. Per read, not per request, so a large slow upload is fine as long as it keeps making progress. `0` disables it.

env.name: IMBH_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT
env.description: On SIGTERM (a `docker plugin disable`), how long in-flight requests and container lines get to finish before the buffer is sealed and the process exits. `0` does not wait. Keep it under the daemon's own stop grace.

env.name: RUST_LOG
env.description: Log filter for imbhd's own diagnostics. Output goes to the Docker daemon log.
